Language workspaces ​

Context ​

ADR#9316364013 reserves the directories that belong to no single language workspace, but it does not say where a language workspace itself lives. A repository that ships a Rust server next to a Go client, an Elixir client and a TypeScript console has to place several toolchains, each with its own manifest, lockfile and tool configuration.

A survey of our repositories found most multi-language repositories already converged on one root directory per toolchain named <language>workspace/: rsworkspace/, goworkspace/, tsworkspace/, pyworkspace/. The language part drifted where nothing fixed it: rustworkspace/ next to go-workspace/ in one repository, elixirworkspace/ next to rsworkspace/ in others. Single-language Rust repositories kept the Cargo workspace at the root.

The language part is fixed here as the language's source file extension, so a new language never needs a naming decision.

Resolution ​

  • You MUST place each language toolchain of a repository with source in more than one language in its own root directory named <extension>workspace/, where <extension> is the language's source file extension without the dot:

    LanguageDirectory
    Rustrsworkspace/
    Gogoworkspace/
    TypeScripttsworkspace/
    Elixirexworkspace/
    Pythonpyworkspace/
    Kotlinktworkspace/
    Swiftswiftworkspace/

  • You MUST NOT spell the language out or separate the words: rustworkspace/, elixirworkspace/, go-workspace/ and go_workspace/ are wrong.

  • You MUST NOT use a bare language name (rust/, go/, elixir/) or a role name (clients/, sdks/, packages/, apps/) at the repository root for source a toolchain builds.

  • You MAY keep the toolchain at the repository root while the repository has source in one language only. You MUST move it into its workspace when a second language arrives.

  • You MUST make each workspace the root of exactly one toolchain: its manifest and lockfile sit directly in it, such as Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock, go.mod or go.work, mix.exs and mix.lock, pnpm-workspace.yaml and pnpm-lock.yaml, pyproject.toml and uv.lock.

  • You SHOULD set the workspace up with the toolchain's own multi-package mechanism, such as a Cargo workspace, a go.work file, a pnpm workspace, a Mix umbrella, a uv workspace or a Gradle multi-project build, with each package in its own directory, even while it holds a single package. A second package then joins the workspace instead of reshaping it. You MAY place a single package directly at the workspace root, such as a single Cargo package whose Cargo.toml declares no [workspace] members.

  • You MUST keep configuration read by one toolchain only, such as clippy.toml, deny.toml, rustfmt.toml, rust-toolchain.toml, .golangci.yaml, .formatter.exs and tsconfig.base.json, in that workspace and MUST NOT keep it at the repository root. Configuration for a tool that reads the whole repository goes under .config/<tool>/.

  • You MUST keep everything a workspace owns inside it, including database migrations its code embeds, test fixtures and examples.

  • You MUST NOT carry a copy of a directory reserved by ADR#9316364013 inside a workspace. The workspace uses the copy its project nests per ADR#0752163629 when there is one, and the repository root copy otherwise.

  • You MUST place the members of a Cargo workspace under crates/<crate>/ relative to the workspace directory, which is rsworkspace/crates/<crate>/ for the root project and projects/<project>/rsworkspace/crates/<crate>/ for a named one. You MUST follow the toolchain's own layout inside every other workspace.

    txt
    .
├── .github/
├── .config/<tool>/
├── devops/
├── docs/
├── proto/
├── otel/
├── rsworkspace
│   ├── Cargo.toml
│   ├── Cargo.lock
│   ├── clippy.toml
│   ├── deny.toml
│   └── crates/<crate>/
├── goworkspace
│   ├── go.work
│   └── <module>/go.mod
├── exworkspace
│   ├── mix.exs           # umbrella
│   ├── mix.lock
│   └── apps/<app>/
└── LICENSE

Consequences ​

  • The module directive in go.mod sets a Go module's import path, not its directory. A module at goworkspace/<module>/ whose path matches its location is imported as github.com/<org>/<repo>/goworkspace/<module> and tags its releases goworkspace/<module>/vX.Y.Z. A repository that publishes a Go module for others to import decides that path before the first release, because changing it later breaks every importer.
  • Existing rustworkspace/, go-workspace/, elixirworkspace/ and kotlinworkspace/ directories are renamed. The rename touches the paths in CI, container builds and mise tasks, and nothing else.
